column1: # Stations of the nav gauntlet, generated by scripts/gauntlet/gen_gauntlet.py.
# `plans` is what the PLANNER does today - measured, not predicted: does A* reach
# the goal at all. It is a regression lock. A change here is a change in what an
# agent will even ATTEMPT, and should always be a deliberate one.
# `expect` is what a vanilla player could do with MOVEMENT AND A HAND - doors,
# gates, hatches, what is beside an iron door; no building. It is design intent, not a
# measurement, and nothing asserts against it; the report scores `plans`
# refusals are correct and which are gaps.
# The stations below marked headless-only are never walked in-world: they share a
# lane's goal pad with the station they are named after, and the in-world score asks
# only whether SOMEBODY is standing on it. One line, ids last - report.py reads it.
# `expectBlocks` and `plansBlocks` are the same two for the second layer, every runner
# carrying a stack of dirt it may lay, its search fenced to its own lane. Last, so they
# shift no column the Java suite parses by index.
